title: Identity law for structure-sheaf cohomology pullback
statement: For every scheme X and n ≥ 0, structureSheafCohomologyPullback (𝟙 X) n = AddMonoidHom.id (Sheaf.H (structureSheafAb X) n).

proof.text: For the identity scheme morphism, the functor on opens and its continuous sheaf pushforward are definitionally the identity. Let adj be the chosen sheaf pullback adjunction and let alpha = adj.leftAdjointUniq Adjunction.id. Applying the adjunction hom equivalence shows that the adjoint of the additive identity structure map equals alpha at the structure sheaf. Applying the hom equivalence for the composed constant-sheaf and pullback adjunctions shows that the hom of constantSheafsheafPullbackIso at the integer group equals alpha at the constant integer sheaf. Both equalities are proved by uniqueness of left adjoints, not assumed.

Prove Ext naturality for any exact additive endofunctor L and natural transformation alpha : L -> Id in a category with enough injectives. In degree zero, represent an Ext class by an ordinary morphism and apply naturality of alpha. In degree n+1, embed the target B into Injective.obj B and form its cokernel short exact sequence S. Ext vanishing into an injective and covariant_sequence_exact₁ express the class as y composed with S.extClass. Alpha induces a morphism S.map L -> S. Apply the existing, proved Adjunction.mapExactFunctor_comp_extClass_comp_mk₀ to this morphism, use the induction hypothesis on y, and reassociate. This induction is fully proved in the private helper ext_map_to_identity.

Unfold structureSheafCohomologyPullback, H.mapFunctor and H.map pointwise. Replace the adjoint structure morphism by alpha at the structure sheaf. Reassociate the Yoneda product, apply the proved Ext naturality helper, and replace alpha at the constant integer sheaf by the hom of the constant-sheaf comparison. Its inverse followed by its hom is the identity; mk₀_comp_mk₀_assoc and mk₀_id_comp therefore return the original Ext class. AddMonoidHom extensionality gives the identity homomorphism in every degree.
